messages:
jess: Quick question — I'm adding a new Terraform module that creates an ArgoCD App for analytics-service. Need to wire GH Actions + Atlantis + ArgoCD so we don't have ArgoCD trying to sync a half-applied manifest. Also need to handle repo creds (KMS across accounts). What's the recommended gating pattern?

mike: short answer: ensure Atlantis apply finishes and artifacts are stable before ArgoCD sees the new app. Two common patterns: artifactize manifests (S3/GCS) after apply, or gate ArgoCD via a webhook/flag that is flipped by the CI job once apply is done. :white_check_mark:

sofia: +1 to artifact approach for infra -> app handoff. If ArgoCD points at the git repo that Atlantis updates, you can get races when apply updates k8s resources but the manifests in git are partially updated. Artifactization avoids that.

samir: If you want to keep it git-native, consider a GH Action that: runs Atlantis plan/apply (or waits for Atlantis apply), then runs a short "post-apply validation" (kustomize build && kubectl apply --server-dry-run) and then creates a small marker file in a dedicated branch/path that ArgoCD watches. ArgoCD will only sync when marker exists.

jess: any examples of the GH Action wait-for-atlantis step?

mike: here's a simple snippet we used before — Atlantis posts a comment with apply status, so GH Action polls the PR comments and proceeds when it sees "atlantis apply: finished". crude but reliable:

```yaml
- name: wait for atlantis apply
  uses: actions/github-script@v6
  with:
    script: |
      const { owner, repo } = context.repo
      const pr = process.env.PR_NUMBER
      async function check() {
        const comments = await github.issues.listComments({ owner, repo, issue_number: pr })
        return comments.data.some(c => c.body && c.body.includes('atlantis apply finished'))
      }
      for (let i=0;i<30;i++) {
        if (await check()) return
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10000))
      }
      throw new Error('timed out waiting for atlantis apply')
```

mike: after that step, you can trigger an ArgoCD webhook or push a small marker file that the ArgoCD app watches.

sofia: note on locks: Atlantis project locks prevent concurrent applies to the same project, but they don't prevent ArgoCD from seeing a mid-state while resources reconcile. That's why the marker/artifact is safer.

samir: about secrets/cross-account KMS: we usually encrypt repo creds with SOPS using an AWS KMS key in the infra account. For the cluster side (ArgoCD repo creds), replicate the secret into the target account/namespace via a short sync job or use ExternalSecrets + cross-account IAM role to fetch from Secrets Manager. Example assume-role: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/InfraReadOnly --role-session-name argocd-sync`

jess: is there any preferred approach for the repo URL: point ArgoCD at the same git branch Atlantis touches, or to the artifact store?

mike: artifact store if you want absolute determinism. Git is fine if you can guarantee atomic commits and a gating marker. We had a bug where ArgoCD saw a new kustomize kustomization before generated secrets were fully in place — artifact + post-apply validation would have avoided it.

sofia: small ops tip: add a short health-check job in the GH Action that tries `kubectl get pods -n analytics -l app=analytics --context prod` (or dry-run) before flipping the marker. That catches obvious failures early.

samir: if you go artifact route, store artifact path with a commit id and let ArgoCD app use the manifest path (not raw repo). We use S3 + signed URL TTL to avoid leakage.

jess: ok cool. I'll draft a GH Action that: checkout -> trigger atlantis plan (comment) -> wait for atlantis apply (poll comments) -> post-apply validation -> upload manifests to S3 -> create marker file for ArgoCD. I'll throw the draft in a PR in infra repo for review. Anyone want to review once I have a draft? :eyes:

mike: happy to review, ping me in the PR.

sofia: I'll take a look at the secrets wiring. Recommend adding KMS key policy + delegated role docs.

deploy-bot: Heads-up: when you create the ArgoCD App, include `syncPolicy.automated: false` initially so manual validation can occur.

atlantis-bot: Atlantis: project locked on PR #412 for apply in progress.

jess: thanks all — will post PR shortly and @mike @sofia for reviews.

mike: :thumbsup:
